An accurate determination of the final relic abundance therefore requires a consistent treatment of both continued production and entropy dilution. We further examine the impact of scalar cubic interactions and find that they modify the boundaries between the different production regimes and reshape the relic-density contours. In particular, the results are more sensitive to the cubic coupling involving the mediator and the light scalar than to the heavy-scalar self-coupling.

papers.title: Landscape of Higgs vacua in 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$
papers.abstract: Strongly coupled 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories have a Higgs branch of their moduli space of vacua, identified by 1/2-BPS operators and their algebraic relations. For $SU(N_c)_k$ theories, we map the moduli space across different phases and we establish how the Chern-Simons level $k$ deforms the chiral ring relations among mesons, baryons, and instantons, while determining specific patterns of symmetry enhancement. For $SO(N_c)$ theories, we construct the corresponding chiral ring constraints at infinite coupling. Finally, we identify the Higgs branch as a classical integrable system, through the expansion of the chiral ring in terms of action variables.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous balanced non-Kähler metrics on complex projective spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the cohomogeneity one action of $G_{p,q}=\mathrm{U}(p+1)\times\mathrm{U}(q+1)$ on $\mathbb{C}P^{p+q+1}$, where $p\geq q\geq 1$ and $p>1$. We characterize all $G_{p,q}$-invariant Riemannian metrics compatible with the canonical complex structure and obtain parametrizations of the invariant Kähler and balanced metrics. As an application, we use these parametrizations to construct a family of inhomogeneous balanced non-Kähler metrics with positive scalar curvature on complex projective spaces of odd complex dimension.

papers.title: Topological deformations of local gauge theories: a presymplectic BV-AKSZ approach
papers.abstract: The same local degrees of freedom can be described by systems with different gauge structure and field content. Standard examples are the duality between the scalar field and the 2-form gauge field in four dimensions, and unimodular gravity, where the cosmological constant becomes a global degree of freedom. In a precise sense, the spaces of gauge-inequivalent formal solutions of such systems differ by a finite-dimensional sector. Moreover, because their gauge sectors are different, their consistent interactions and their sensitivity to the global structure of spacetime may differ substantially. We show that such systems are naturally related by what we call topological deformations: gauging a symmetry of generic degree couples the system to a BF-type sector without introducing new local degrees of freedom. The construction is carried out systematically within the presymplectic BV-AKSZ approach, where it amounts to a modification of the underlying presymplectic gauge PDE. Gauging degree-0 symmetries identifies solutions related by global symmetries, which reproduces the scalar--2-form and principal chiral model--Freedman--Townsend dualities. Gauging degree-1 symmetries, i.e. deformations, gives rise to new global degrees of freedom, such as the cosmological constant in unimodular gravity.

papers.title: Wrapping M5-branes on a non-spin manifold: Spin$^h$ structures and AdS$_7$ black holes
papers.abstract: We construct a solution of seven-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_5$, where $M_5$ is the five-dimensional Wu manifold $SU(3)/SO(3)$. The solution is supersymmetric, despite the fact that the Wu manifold admits neither a spin structure nor a spin$^c$ structure. Rather, it admits a spin$^h$ structure, wherein the ill-definedness of ordinary spinors due to a minus sign in their holonomy is compensated by a further minus sign arising through the spinors carrying $SO(3)$ Yang-Mills charge, in a half-integer isospin representation of the $SU(2)$ double cover of the $SO(3)$. We show how the configuration can be lifted to a solution of $D=11$ supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_9$, where $M_9$ is the unit tangent bundle of the Wu manifold. We discuss the geometry and topology of $M_9$, and study the supersymmetry from the eleven-dimensional standpoint. We extend the seven-dimensional solution to a black hole, and discuss some aspects of its holographic interpretation and the UV to IR flow. We revisit a previously-known AdS$_2\times H^3\times H^2$ solution, and its UV to IR flow, showing that the flow equations in fact admit of an exact solution. Additionally, we give a detailed discussion of the lift of the AdS$_2\times S^5$ solution to $D=11$, exhibiting similarities and differences between the properties of its internal space $M_9$ (the unit tangent bundle of $S^5$) and the Wu manifold example of our main discussion. We also construct the non-compact dual of the Wu manifold solution, where $M_5$ is taken to be $SL(3,\mathbb R)/SO(3)$.

papers.title: Breaking the axion abundance-isocurvature relation: Scale invariance and high-scale inflation
papers.abstract: A QCD axion accounting for dark matter through pre-inflationary misalignment is strongly constrained by CMB isocurvature bounds, which place the classic axion window in tension with high-scale inflation. The tension arises because the same decay constant controls both the relic abundance and the primordial axion fluctuations. We show how this link can be broken in a broad class of scale-invariant models, without introducing any dimensionful parameter into the classical action. Rather than imposing a fixed Peccei-Quinn scale, the axion's kinetic normalisation is set by a dynamical field ratio. The resulting field-space metric controls the abundance through its value today and the primordial fluctuations through its value at horizon crossing. A sufficiently large metric during inflation suppresses isocurvature, allowing high-scale inflation in the classic axion window with an untuned misalignment angle and sub-Planckian decay constants. The exact scale and Peccei-Quinn symmetries also enforce a non-turning inflationary attractor, conserving the super-Hubble curvature perturbation and preserving the single-field adiabatic spectrum. We realise the mechanism in the Higgs-Dilaton model by deforming the Peccei-Quinn kinetic term. The same deformation turns the inflaton sector into an $α$-attractor pinned near the Starobinsky point. This explicit realisation has a super-Planckian present decay constant, which places it in the anthropic window, now reopened at high inflationary scales, with an ultralight QCD axion constrained by black-hole superradiance.

papers.title: Multimessenger Probes of Primordial Black Holes with Gravitational Wave and 21 cm Observations
papers.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from the collapse of curvature perturbations in the early universe are known to have an associated gravitational wave signal sourced by the same scalar perturbations. In this work, we show that there is a complementarity between these gravitational waves and modifications of the 21 cm global signal during the cosmic dark ages due to PBH evaporation. For PBHs in the range $ M_{\rm PBH} \sim 5 \times 10^{13} \, {\rm g} - 10^{17} \, {\rm g}$, there is a correlated signal in gravitational waves in the LISA, deci-Hz, and ground based regimes from $f_{\rm GW} \sim 10^{-3} \, {\rm Hz} - 20 \, {\rm Hz}$ and in the 21 cm global signal from $z \sim 300 - 30$. These observations are entirely independent of each other and within the reach of near-future experiments, making a combined measurement a novel multimessenger probe of primordial physics.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves as a Probe of Multi-Fluid Cosmologies: General Formalism and the Case of Cosmological Stasis
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) provide a powerful probe of the expansion history of the universe prior to the Big Bang. Indeed, the production of such gravity waves depends on the evolution of first-order scalar perturbations within the early universe, while their subsequent propagation depends on the background equation of state. In this paper we extend previous discussions by studying SIGWs in cosmologies containing multiple fluids. As we shall demonstrate, the gravitational-wave signal within such multi-fluid cosmologies is modified in two distinct ways: not only are there new velocity effects which have no single-fluid analogues, but there are also significant alterations to the subsequent redshifting of modes that enter the horizon before the multi-fluid era ends. Thus SIGWs provide a probe of not only the overall expansion rate within such cosmologies, but also their internal multi-fluid composition. As an example, we then consider the case of gravitational waves arising during an epoch of cosmological stasis. During such an epoch, the abundances of energy components with different equations of state remain constant, thereby giving rise to a universe with a constant effective equation of state which nevertheless remains genuinely multi-fluid despite cosmological expansion. Despite their constant equations of state, we find that such stasis cosmologies also give rise to tensor power spectra and present-day gravitational-wave abundances which are significantly different from those expected within a standard radiation-dominated universe.

papers.title: Symplectic Lie groups and nilmanifolds associated with acyclic quivers
papers.abstract: We give combinatorial criteria for the existence of left-invariant symplectic forms on the positive and full path Lie groups of finite acyclic quivers. For the nilpotent positive path Lie groups, the criterion also determines whether their compact quotients admit symplectic forms and forces the nilpotency step to be at most three. For the completely solvable full path Lie groups, we give a direct combinatorial criterion and an equivalent recursive criterion. In the symplectic case, the recursive procedure is realized by successive Hamiltonian reductions ending at an abelian symplectic Lie group. We characterize the existence of Lagrangian normal subgroups for a given form in both families, with applications to Lagrangian torus fibrations of compact nilmanifolds. We also describe the cohomology rings of the compact symplectic nilmanifolds and determine all Lefschetz ranks.

papers.title: Mass, forces, and the dark sector in a Kaluza-Klein model with 6 compact dimensions
papers.abstract: (1) Objective: This study seeks to calculate the meson and baryon masses and to investigate the dynamics within hadrons and lepton pairs by formulating a unified physical framework that, in addition to gravitation, simultaneously incorporates the strong, electromagnetic and weak interactions. (2) Method: A framework inspired by the Standard Model and based on Kaluza-Klein theory is formulated using an extended general-relativistic description in a spacetime of one temporal, three spatial, and six compactified dimensions. The model suggests that excitations, deformations of the 10-dimensional spacetime traveling at light-speed, contribute to mass and distinct spin characteristics in a 4-dimensional setting. Using the electron g-factor, charged-lepton masses, and masses of the proton, neutron, and neutral and charged pion, neutral and charged rho, phi, psi, upsilon mesons, the parameters compactification radius rho, weak interaction coupling alpha_w, strong interaction coupling alpha_s, flavor constants A_i and the antineutrino/neutrino density ratio delta3 are determined and used to compute the masses of the hadrons. (3) Key results: Masses of 102 hadrons are obtained; comparison with data from 71 measurements shows relative errors below 0.05 in 70%, below 0.1 in 89% and below 0.2 in 100%, with a correlation coefficient r=0.997 between the measured and calculated masses. Thirty-one additional hadron masses are predicted, and the model identifies asymmetries in electric and weak forces, as well as distance- and velocity-dependent interactions. (4) Implications: The framework offers testable predictions for hadron spectroscopy, predicts sterile, exclusive gravitationally interacting bosons as dark-matter candidates, states the equations for the elementary forces, and suggests possible connections between force asymmetries and dark energy.

papers.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
papers.abstract: In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point. Here, we deform the holographic dipole model so that its two coalescing scaling dimensions split into either two real ones or a complex-conjugate pair. We obtain the renormalized two-point functions in closed form. They change continuously from a linear combination of two power laws, through the logarithmic form of the LCFT at the exceptional point, to log-periodic oscillations. For any pair of scalar primary operators with real mixing under dilatations, the conformal Ward identities fix this form up to two normalization constants, which the holographic dictionary determines. In PT-symmetric theories with such a dilatation operator, real and complex-conjugate scaling dimensions correspond to the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases. In the BTZ black hole at finite temperature, the difference between the quasinormal frequencies associated with the two scaling dimensions changes from purely imaginary to purely real across the real-to-complex spectral transition. Correspondingly, the linear response changes from overdamped to underdamped, with critical damping at the exceptional point.

papers.title: The metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron: parameter-free inflation
papers.abstract: We present a model of slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity, where the connection is independent of the metric. We require that the Einstein-Hilbert term is the only operator that breaks three out of four shift-symmetries of the connection, and impose them on the metric-affine Starobinsky term $αR(Γ)^2$. This replaces it by $α\mathring{R}^2$, the square of the invariant part of the scalar curvature. The theory propagates only the graviton and one healthy scalar, the metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron. Its potential approaches a plateau polynomially, $U\simeq U_0(1-μ^2/χ^2)$, with $μ=\sqrt{6}\,M_P$ fixed by the curvature of the connection. Once $α\simeq2\times10^{8}$ is set by the scalar amplitude, the model has no free parameters. It predicts $n_s\simeq1-3/(2N_*)$ and $r\simeq2\sqrt3\,N_*^{-3/2}$ at leading order in $N_*$, and $n_s=0.968$--$0.974$ and $r=0.011$-$0.008$ with exact slow-roll for $N_*=50$-$60$ $e$-folds. These values agree with current data, and $r$ is within reach of the next generation of $B$-mode measurements.

papers.title: Optical conductivity of holographic striped superconductors
papers.abstract: Based on a holographic model exhibiting Mott-like insulating behavior on an ionic lattice, we construct a holographic striped superconductor (SSC), which is characterized by the interplay between the charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity (SC). We present the phase diagram on the $e$-$T$ plane, where the SSC phase emerges within an intermediate window of $e$, revealing both cooperative and competitive relations between the CDW order and SC order. For small charge $e$, the system undergoes the phase transition from metallic phase to CDW phase, and then to SSC phase upon cooling; while for large $e$, it transitions from metallic phase to SC phase directly, and then to SSC phase. We compute the optical conductivity of the system for these two cases and demonstrate its distinct behavior. It turns out that the imaginary part of the conductivity exhibits a divergent behavior below the critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{SSC}}$ along both pathways, so that the superconductivity of SSC phase is justified for the first time in the holographic framework. Along the CDW-to-SSC pathway the pseudogap and the pinning effect are inherited from the CDW phase, whereas along the SC-to-SSC pathway the spontaneous stripe strongly suppresses the coherent normal-fluid channel while the superfluid pole is enhanced. In addition, we demonstrate the commensurate lock-in behavior of the striped superconductor in the $p$-$T$ diagram.

papers.title: Noncommutative $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities
papers.abstract: We derive $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups on finite von Neumann algebras, from a spectral gap (PI) or from a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (MLSI). For $p\ge2$, the corresponding coefficients have optimal order $O(p)$ and $O(\sqrt p)$, respectively. Both estimates follow from Beckner inequalities by integration along semigroups. We also establish a non-tracial extension to quantum Markov semigroups satisfying GNS detailed balance. As a direct byproduct, we apply $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities to Schatten-valued functions on graphs in order to obtain the Schatten distortion of expanders.

papers.title: Anisotropic hadronic matter in external magnetic fields
papers.abstract: Strong magnetic fields generated in non-central heavy-ion collisions break rotational symmetry and can imprint anisotropy on the produced quantum chromodynamics (QCD) matter. Within a hadron resonance gas framework in the presence of an external magnetic field, we investigate the resulting anisotropy in the equation of state, isothermal compressibility, speed of sound, and conserved-charge fluctuations. We find that the electric-charge susceptibility ratio $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q$ develops a pronounced directional dependence, driven primarily by the Landau-level structure of charged pions. For physically relevant magnetic fields, this anisotropy reaches $\sim 10 - 15 \%$ at $T\simeq0.16$ GeV. The ratio of electric-charge susceptibility can be expressed as $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q=C_4^Q/C_2^Q=κ_Qσ_Q^2$, where $C_2^Q$ and $C_4^Q$ are the second- and fourth-order cumulants, and $κ_Q$ and $σ_Q$ are the kurtosis and variance of the event-by-event net-electric-charge distribution. The reaction-plane dependence of this ratio provides an experimentally accessible signature of magnetic-field-induced anisotropy. Our results identify higher-order electric-charge fluctuations as a promising probe of the imprint of strong electromagnetic fields on the matter produced in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC.

papers.title: Ricci pinching on complete Kähler manifolds with nonnegative bisectional curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that a connected complete Kähler manifold of complex dimension at least two with nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature and uniformly pinched Ricci curvature is compact or flat. This removes the Euclidean volume growth assumption from the flatness theorem of Liu and Ni \cite{LiuNi} for uniform Ricci pinching. We first construct a Lipschitz plurisubharmonic function with finite total Monge--Ampère mass by solving a global Bellman equation. Weighted estimates for a holomorphic canonical section then give a finite top Ricci integral. Ricci pinching implies that the Ricci form belongs to $L^n$, and its Hodge heat evolution has zero top integral by a Stokes argument and scalar heat decay. \par\noindent\textit{Keywords.} Kähler manifolds, Ricci pinching, nonnegative bisectional curvature, Bellman equations, Monge--Ampère mass.

papers.title: Type I estimates for the Kähler-Ricci flow II
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish geometric consequences of our Type I scalar curvature estimate for finite-time solutions of the Kähler-Ricci flow on compact Kähler manifolds. We prove a uniform global diameter bound and a Type I diameter bound for every fibre of finite time holomorphic contraction. These estimates yield Gromov-Hausdorff convergence to a unique compact metric space homeomorphic to the normal Kähler space determined by the limiting cohomology class. We also establish a local partial $C^0$ estimate for the normalized flow and show that the tangent shrinkers are normal complex analytic varieties with log terminal singularities.

papers.title: Constraints on Decaying Dark Matter with $B=1$ from Fermi-LAT
papers.abstract: We investigate the gamma ray signatures of fermionic dark matter that carries one unit of baryon number and decays into three quarks. We compute the expected prompt and secondary gamma-ray spectra for a representative range of final state flavor combinations. By comparing these spectra to Fermi-LAT measurements of the isotropic gamma-ray background, we derive exclusion limits on the lifetime. We observe that depending on the dark matter mass and the flavor of the final state, the lifetime bounds on decays of $B=1$ dark matter can differ by up to a factor of two from those on decays of $B=0$ dark matter. Furthermore, light-quark final states generally yield stronger bounds at lower masses, whereas heavy-quark final states can yield comparable or stronger bounds at masses of tens of TeV and above.

papers.title: Superstring theory in $AdS_5\times S^5$ background: half-BPS vertex operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct all vertex operators associated with the gravity supermultiplet in the $AdS_5 \times S^5$ background, relevant for worldsheet scattering amplitude computations, via global $PSU(2,2|4)$ transformations. Although one such operator was previously constructed in the pure spinor formalism using a special superspace parametrization, implementing the full global symmetries proved challenging due to the mixing of bosonic and fermionic coordinates. We resolve this issue by introducing a judicious sequence of reparametrizations that disentangle these coordinates. We then advance the formulation of superstring theory in this background by constructing the corresponding integrated vertex operators in both the pure spinor and the B-RNS-GSS formalisms.

papers.title: A non-prompt null ray cures its own singularity
papers.abstract: In AdS/CFT correlators, bulk cone singularities arise when two points that are timelike separated on the AdS boundary may be connected by a null geodesic through the bulk. We consider corrections to these correlators away from the $G_N\to 0$ limit arising from the backreaction of this null geodesic. A peculiar property of this geodesic is that it is not prompt, meaning that there exist points on it that are timelike separated. This implies that it may gravitationally affect itself. We show that this leads to an energy-dependent delay in the time elapsed along this geodesic. This coupled with possible inelastic effects due to gravitational radiation are the leading mechanisms that resolve the singularity. The resolved singularity is accompanied by oscillations and hence zeroes in the real and imaginary parts of the correlator. We comment on the role that additional inelastic effects play in damping these oscillations. Finally, we provide a concrete example in $2+1$D where we can compute the energy-dependent time delay effect explicitly by studying the boundary graviton mode.

papers.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
papers.abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.

papers.title: Extending Donaldson's HyperKähler Structure via Minimal Surfaces into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$
papers.abstract: We construct a deformation space for minimal immersions into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ with its holomorphic Killing form, and define an explicit, mapping class group invariant, complex hyperKähler structure on such deformation space. Such complex hyperKähler structure restricts to: Donaldson's hyperKähler structure on a totally real copy of almost-Fuchsian space, Mazzoli-Seppi-Tamburelli's para-hyperKähler structure on a totally real copy of maximally globally hyperbolic $\mathbb{A}\mathrm{d}\mathbb{S}^3$ manifolds, and Loustau-Sanders' complex bi-Kähler structure on a holomorphic copy of quasi-Fuchsian space. Moreover, all these loci are totally geodesic. We discuss other geometric aspects of this space, such as the Hamiltonian property of a natural $\mathbb{C}^*$-action, involving the Goldman symplectic form and a complex-valued area functional.

papers.title: Spurious Singularities in Dipole Subtraction Cross Sections and their Damping with Convergence Factors
papers.abstract: In the dipole subtraction algorithm, the real-virtual cancellation in NLO calculations of arbitrary observables is implemented by defining a subtraction cross section that matches all of the singularities of the real emission cross section. The converse, however, is not true: the subtraction cross section contains additional singularities, coming from the underlying Born matrix element, that the real cross section does not. We call these spurious singularities. If used as originally proposed, this is not a problem, because the value of the observable damps these singularities, but in applications such as dipole showers and matching algorithms, it can lead to poor statistical convergence, or dependence on unphysical regulators such as technical or generation cuts. In this paper, we show that additional factors, which we call convergence factors, can be applied to the subtraction cross section to damp these spurious singularities and improve the convergence. We perform the required phase-space integrals to yield modified dipole insertion operators, and verify numerically that they indeed remove the logarithmic dependence on generation cuts that arises in their absence. This paper is dedicated to the memory of Stefano Catani, with whom the work was originally started.

papers.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
papers.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff Convergence of Constant Scalar Curvature Kähler Metrics near the Canonical Class
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-ample canonical bundle. For any Kähler class $[ω]$, Jian--Shi--Song proved that there exists a unique cscK metric in the class $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ when $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$, using the properness criterion of Chen--Cheng. We prove that the cscK metrics in $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ converge, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology to the metric completion of the twisted Kähler-Einstein metric on the canonical model of $X$ as conjectured by Jian--Shi--Song. Based on the technique developed in this paper, we can also give a new proof the theorem of Lee--Tosatti--Zhang on the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the normalized Kähler--Ricci flow on $X$.

papers.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
papers.abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

papers.title: Finite Time Noncollapsing Kähler-Ricci Flow: Gaussian Type Heat Kernel, Gromov-Hausdorff Limits
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study heat kernel estimates along the Kähler-Ricci flow with finite time noncollapsing singularities over a compact Kähler manifold. The starting point is the type-II scalar-curvature estimate, which gives the natural parabolic scale $r\lesssim T-t$ near the singular time. By combining the distance distortion and space-time cut-off estimates of Bamler--Zhang with entropy, mean-value inequality, and conjugate heat-kernel estimates, we obtain two-sided Gaussian bounds and gradient bounds that are uniform on this scale. Under the global type-I scalar-curvature estimate, the same estimates hold on every scale. We then use these estimates and the monotonicity of the $W_1$-distance between conjugate heat flows to construct a canonical singular-time pseudo-distance. The distances $d_t$ (induced by $ω(t)$) converge uniformly to this pseudo-distance. Its metric quotient is the unique Gromov--Hausdorff limit. Finally, we apply Bamler's theory and the recent work of Hallgren--Zhang to obtain the following. Every fixed-base-point type-I blow-up admits a subsequential metric-flow limit whose time slices are singular shrinking Kähler--Ricci soliton spaces with normal complex-analytic and log-terminal structure, unique tangent cones, and a polarized Fano fibration. For moving base points, the limiting metric flow, equipped with its limiting conjugate heat flow, is a metric soliton precisely under an entropy-pinching condition.

papers.title: Asymptotics of the Moduli Spaces of Parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)$-Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study the large-scale geometry of the moduli spaces of stable strongly parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere for a family of parabolic weights. We glue the local Toda model metric to a decoupled metric obtained from the spectral line bundle, and perturb the resulting approximate metrics to harmonic metrics adapted to the parabolic structure. We also prove that Hitchin's $L^2$ metric approaches the semi-flat metric exponentially. The metric comparison and the spectral period calculation show that each moduli space is a complete ALG gravitational instanton of type $E_6$. The asymptotic estimates are uniform on compact subintervals of the weight chamber.

papers.title: Dark Matter Particle Explorer: Ten-Year On-Orbit Performance and Scientific Outcomes
papers.abstract: The Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE, also known as ``Wukong'') is the first scientific space mission within the framework of the Strategic Pioneer Program on Space Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The main scientific objectives of DAMPE include indirect detection of dark matter, cosmic-ray physics, and high energy gamma-ray astronomy. Thanks to its large geometrical factor and thick imaging calorimeter, DAMPE could effectively detect cosmic-ray electrons (including positrons) and gamma-rays up to 10~TeV, and nuclei up to PeV. Since launched on 17 December 2015 into a Sun-synchronous orbit, DAMPE has been smoothly operating on orbit for more than ten years. Here we present an overview of instrument, on-orbit status, and highlight scientific results of DAMPE, including the measurements of the all-electron energy spectrum and the spectra of protons and other nuclei, and high energy gamma-ray line search.

papers.title: PTagent: An LLM-assisted tool for finite-temperature model construction in cosmological phase transitions
papers.abstract: Cosmological phase-transition calculations require well-defined finite-temperature numerical models, whose construction involves assembling model information under consistent theoretical prescriptions. In this work we present \texttt{PTagent}, a large language model (LLM) agent-based framework for constructing such models from SARAH model files, research papers, and DRalgo sources. The LLM agent interprets and organizes model information and identifies unresolved physical choices, while dedicated backends perform the model-dependent calculations. After review and approval of the resulting physical model specification, the backends generate the corresponding CosmoTransitions-style or PhaseTracer-style numerical potentials. By separating model interpretation from numerical implementation, PTagent provides an inspectable and reproducible approach to finite-temperature model construction for cosmological phase-transition studies.

papers.title: Two-loop HTL-resummed thermodynamics for pure $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: We compute the two-loop hard-thermal-loop (HTL) resummed thermodynamic potential of pure four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory using regularization by dimensional reduction. Our result is gauge invariant and was renormalized using vacuum energy, gluon mass $m_d$ and quark mass $m_q$ counterterms. The thermal mass parameters are determined self-consistently and numerically from gap equations incorporating the running coupling. Based on these solutions, we numerically calculate the scaled pressure, entropy density, energy density, and trace anomaly and compare them with the results in the static perturbative limit through $\mathcal O(λ^2)$. For the first three quantities, next-to-leading-order (NLO) corrections are positive and have discernible effects at small coupling, and reduce the renormalization-scale dependence at relatively large couplings. We assess $m_q$-prescription dependence by comparing these results with those obtained by setting $m_q=0$. We find that it has a substantial impact on $m_d$ and the scalar mass $m_s$ at large couplings, and it reverses the signs of the NLO corrections to the first three quantities and qualitatively alters the trace anomaly.

papers.title: Operator Algebraic Quantum Hypergroups
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of operator algebraic quantum hypergroups and their representations, formulated using a special case of the algebraic quantum hypergroup framework of van Daele and Delvaux. As part of the axioms, every operator algebraic quantum hypergroup admits a dual object of the same type. We prove that a certain universal completion in the compact case satisfies the axioms of an earlier notion of a compact quantum hypergroup in the sense of the second author and Chapovsky. As part of this theory, we discuss their (co)amenability properties. We consider examples induced by conditional expectations of algebraic quantum groups satisfying certain properties, which include quantum hypergroups corresponding to double cosets and automorphisms of quantum groups, and quantum hypergroups induced by representation categories of Kac type compact quantum groups.

papers.title: Local supersymmetry implies momentum map/Gauntlett-Pakis equations and vanishing generalized Komar forms
papers.abstract: The first-order differential equations satisfied by Killing spinor bilinears (momentum map equations or Gauntlett--Pakis equations, Killing vector equations and the vanishing of the generalized Komar charge of the supersymmetric Killing vector) can be derived directly from the action of the local supersymmetry algebra on bosonic fields. We show how this comes about in several examples of increasing complexity, one of which is 11-dimensional supergravity.

papers.title: Symplectic groupoid multiplication and Poisson integrators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the role of local symplectic groupoid multiplication in the construction of approximation methods for Hamiltonian flows on the underlying Poisson manifold. We show it can be used to construct a novel multiplicative type of approximating sequences for the relevant Lagrangian bisection. We describe the corresponding theoretical results, their practical implementation into approximation methods on coordinate charts via generating functions, and illustrative examples.

papers.title: Cosmology & Astrophysics of the Dark Dimension with Bulk Majorana Neutrinos
papers.abstract: Recently, the possibility of having sterile Majorana neutrinos charged under $B-L$ gauge symmetry in the bulk of the dark dimension has been explored. We point out a cosmological restriction on the Majorana mass of bulk neutrinos leading to mass $\gtrsim 100~{\rm GeV}$. This avoids the over-production of Kaluza-Klein neutrino towers in the early universe thus resolving the cosmological neutrino catastrophe of extra dimension scenarios. If the mass of the bulk neutrino is at the lower end of this bound, it can potentially also explain the recently observed Fermi halo excess on gamma rays through the evaporation of long-lived 5d (i.e. dark) black holes through Hawking radiation to bulk neutrinos, which promptly decay into standard model particles.

papers.title: Beyond the polynomial ansatz: regular $AdS_3\times M_8$ solutions of M-theory
papers.abstract: We study regular compact solutions of the cohomogeneity-one $AdS_3\times M_8$ system of Gauntlett, Mac Conamhna, Mateos and Waldram, where $M_8$ is an $S^2$ bundle over three constant-curvature Riemann surfaces. We find that an endpoint argument rules out every non-flat curvature-sign sector without a positive-curvature factor, while an analytic deformation gives regular families with four radial shape parameters in all remaining sectors, with the base geometry held fixed. The known polynomial solutions form a proper analytic locus in these families. Non-polynomiality is therefore generic in parameter space, although the deviation from an endpoint-matching polynomial can be very small. Apart from the completely flat exception, the curvature-sign criterion is necessary and sufficient within this ansatz. Four magnetic flux ratios give local coordinates near the reference solution and its small-curvature deformations, and a rational inverse reconstructs candidate endpoint data directly from finite flux ratios. In the fully positive sector we prove that one explicit four-dimensional finite-ratio neighbourhood lies inside the physical flux image. The magnetic periods and leading holographic central charge reduce to endpoint data, and, once the common Brown--Henneaux normalization is fixed, the nontrivial flux dependence of the equivariant localization formula agrees with the endpoint result as an exact algebraic identity. We also quantify the non-polynomial corrections and analyse finite degenerations under explicit convergence hypotheses.

papers.title: Auditing anapole dark matter: the limits of model independence in dark matter effective field theory
papers.abstract: Effective field theory is a powerful tool for studying the low-energy behavior of dark sector models without explicit dependence on the high-energy physics. However, bottom-up EFT analyses can miss important processes in UV completions that are relevant for dark matter production and detection. In this work we demonstrate explicitly that for Majorana dark matter coupled to the photon by the dimension-six anapole operator, different UV completions make qualitatively different predictions at high energy colliders, in the early universe, and in direct detection experiments. Additionally, we show that competitive, and in some cases, leading constraints on anapole dark matter can be derived by searching for signatures of additional particles in the UV completion rather than direct probes of the DM itself. We argue that the UV completions studied in this work have categorically different phenomenologies and that `model-independent' EFT constraints are not always applicable.

papers.title: From Flow-Box Invariants to Global Conservation Laws: Machine Learning-Assisted Detection of Singularities and Near-Integrability
papers.abstract: Conservation laws reveal invariant structure in dynamical systems and constrain their evolution to lower-dimensional level sets. Locally, however, per the flow-box theorem, every $d$-dimensional system generically admits $d-1$ functionally independent conservation laws near a regular point even though, generically, only a few such laws persist globally. Data-driven methods typically learn conservation laws on a prescribed region of phase space from which training samples are drawn, leaving their behavior beyond that region unresolved. We formulate this local-to-global continuation problem and develop an {expanding-domain neural deflation} framework that tracks the number of independent conservation laws over nested domains. The method recovers the expected $d-1$ local invariants and detects their successive breakdown as the domain expands, relaxing to the expected global conservation law limit. It distinguishes the local invariants (associated with Frobenius integrability) from persistent global structure and shows that the domain scale over which additional laws survive reflects proximity to Liouville integrability. Pointwise losses can localize isolated obstructions, whereas in more complicated dynamics the breakdown of our loss functions is gradual and spatially diffuse. The framework thus provides a data-driven approach for studying the persistence and breakdown of (so-far-learned) conservation laws across phase space.

papers.title: Injection of Space Radiation Errors on Low-power NVM using Generative Deep Learning
papers.abstract: We develop an error model for a Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) device that represents the effects of physical faults experienced in a CubeSat mission in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). The CubeSat carries an off-the-shelf low-power Ferroelectric RAM (FRAM) chip and runs repeated read/write tests according to a predefined pattern. We compare every memory snapshot received from the satellite with a reference bitmap to identify bit errors. We visually analyze erroneous values distributions in the memory snapshots and we understand that they are frequently distributed according to regular spatial patterns. We define a generative deep learning technique to automatically learn these spatial patterns and to synthetically generate additional error patterns mimicking the observed ones. The model is capable at producing memory errors for general application-level experimentation. Our preliminary validation indicates that when comparing the model output with the data we collect, 0.92 of the generated bit flips correspond to bit flips in the memory snapshots and the model captures 0.91 of the observed bit flips. A comparison of the spatial distribution of bit flips in 10,000 generated error patterns also provides a Wasserstein distance of 0.073, indicating that the two distributions differ by roughly 7% of the maximum possible displacement of their probability masses.

papers.title: CIS-Transolver: A Cross-Layer Incremental-State Neural Operator for Fine-Scale Automotive Aerodynamic Flow Prediction
papers.abstract: Neural operators offer an efficient data-driven approach to rapid prediction of complex automotive aerodynamic flows. However, spectral bias and other factors limit accurate reconstruction of fine-scale flow variations near complex geometries. Existing studies improve the representation and fitting of fine-scale information mainly through information extraction and training objectives. Further study is needed to determine how extracted local details can be used continually in subsequent operator computations and contribute effectively to the overall flow-field representation. We propose CIS-Transolver, a cross-layer incremental-state neural operator that extends fine-scale modeling from local information extraction to its use across layers. The method extracts fine-scale information through local multiscale analysis and encodes it as geometric moment states that are propagated and updated across layers. By combining information from previous layers with feedback to the value representations in Physics-Attention, the method allows local details to contribute continually to subsequent modeling of global physical correlations. We systematically evaluate CIS-Transolver on three public automotive aerodynamics benchmarks, ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, covering surface pressure fields and volumetric pressure and velocity fields. CIS-Transolver achieves the lowest mean relative L2 error among the evaluated methods for all five prediction metrics across the three benchmarks. The relative error reductions average 8.72% across the five metrics compared with the best baseline for each metric, reaching 16.38% for ShapeNet-Car pressure prediction and 15.60% for AhmedML velocity prediction. These results provide a new approach to fine-scale flow prediction for complex geometries.

papers.title: Learning without relearning physical symmetry: an SO(3)-equivariant convolutional network (CNN) on the sphere
papers.abstract: Many of the most important datasets in the physical sciences live natively on the sphere, and these data often carry no preferred position or orientation. Using methods that do not reflect this symmetry leads to far higher simulation requirements, which can be catastrophic for scientific analyses (forcing reliance on cheap, imperfect models that bias results). We present a novel spherical implementation of a gauge equivariant mesh architecture that is specifically designed for the Hierarchical Equal Area isoLatitude Pixelization (\healpix{}) of the sphere. The $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-equivariant convolution is built from steerable filters, parallel transport and spin-weighted features. The architecture supplies the exact symmetry, so the network does not spend training data learning it. The convolution operations are constructed to give provably exact equivariance, given a band-limit. Our full CNNs can achieve SO(3)-invariance error at per-cent-level and lower, which is controlled through well-understood hyperparameters. On benchmarks, our technique gives the most accurate dense gradient regression and competitive cosmic microwave background foreground removal and denoising. The improved simulation efficiency matters most in simulation-based inference (SBI), where high-fidelity simulations are expensive and neural compressors require large training sets, so a fixed budget forces analyses with less accurate simulators. In cosmology lensing SBI, our technique yields the tightest posteriors at matched simulation count. This approach is a novel method that will enable new convolutional neural network analyses, including generative and inference tasks, for processes and data on the sphere.

papers.title: Sampling the XY model with an attention-based neural network
papers.abstract: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The architecture is combined with physics-informed ingredients: locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities. The resulting sampler significantly outperforms existing neural samplers. We train the model on lattices up to $96\times96$, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.

papers.title: Neural Expansion: A Unified Mechanism for How Deep Neural Networks Generalize
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks demonstrate remarkable generalization despite being highly over-parameterized, challenging traditional statistical learning theories. While several theoretical paradigms such as margin-based bounds, PAC-Bayesian analyses, and neural tangent kernels provide global explanations, they often lack mechanistic insight into how generalization emerges from training dynamics. We introduce Neural Expansion, a unified geometric framework that characterizes generalization through the expansion of directionally-selective ray coverage in the input space. Using Generalization Intervals (GIs), we quantify direction-specific regions around training samples where the model's predictions remain stable. Our extensive empirical studies across diverse architectures and datasets reveal that training leads to progressive expansion of ray coverage, particularly along directions with low Jacobian singular values. This mechanism helps explain a large fraction of correctly classified test inputs, adversarial examples, and even mislabeled or out-of-distribution samples through the geometry of ray coverage rather than instance-level memorization. By connecting input-space curvature to predictive behavior, our framework provides a mechanistic foundation that complements existing global theories of deep learning.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility
papers.abstract: Muon has emerged as a strong optimizer for neural network training and admits an interpretation as steepest descent under a spectral-norm geometry. Yet we find that Muon-trained Transformers can degrade sharply when their MLP hidden channels are pruned after training. To reconcile Muon's optimization performance with structured compressibility, we introduce Budget Muon (BMuon), which modifies Muon's spectral geometry so that hidden channels across blocks compete for a shared allocation budget. The resulting oracle is exactly normalized steepest descent under a family of norms that interpolate between Muon's geometry and structured sparse geometries. Our principal sparsity control is an interpretable global channel-allocation budget, rather than a setting-dependent sparsity-penalty coefficient. For linear factorization models, we show that Muon admits minimum-cost exact representations with redundant hidden width, whereas under the BMuon oracle geometry and a sufficiently scarce budget, every minimum-cost representation is width-minimal. For practical training, we derive a minorization-maximization surrogate for the exact allocation problem. On ImageNet-1K with ViT-S/16, BMuon improves over Muon under gradual structured MLP pruning, and its learned allocations provide a more effective pruning criterion than weight magnitude. On a 1B-parameter LLaMA-style model trained on FineWeb, BMuon improves over Muon under post-training MLP channel pruning.

papers.title: A Class of Rényi-based Concentration Metrics for Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry in Multilayer Perceptrons
papers.abstract: The interpretability of artificial intelligence models has become a central concern, especially for black-box models such as multilayer perceptrons (MLPs). Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry has recently emerged as a framework for analysing the internal representations of these networks, by examining how the hidden layer locally responds to changes in the input through the minors of its Jacobian. The degree to which a few of these minors dominate the rest, known as their concentration, has so far been measured with the Participation Ratio. Although this metric has useful properties, its maximum value depends on the size of the network, so a given value cannot be read as high or low concentration without reference to the architecture. To overcome this limitation, in this paper we propose the $α$-RC metrics, a family of Rényi-based concentration measures that compare the normalized magnitudes of the minors with the uniform distribution through the Rényi divergence of order $α$. All the metrics in the family are bounded between 0 and 1 regardless of the architecture, with 0 indicating that the magnitude is evenly spread over the minors and 1 that it is carried by a single one. Moreover, the metrics are non-decreasing in $α$, and for $α$ = 2 they reduce to an explicit transformation of the Participation Ratio. Computational experiments with single-hidden-layer MLPs trained on a synthetic dataset show the benefits of our proposal.

papers.title: Learning Changes the World and Then What Was Learned has Changed: Training and Deploying Neural Networks in the Control Loop
papers.abstract: Neural networks offer critical adaptability for controlling complex systems where nominal modeling proves intractable. However, when offline-trained neural networks are deployed within closed-loop control systems, their actions fundamentally alter the state distribution upon which they were trained. This paper introduces a unified taxonomy to categorize these sequential failure modes: the initial Closed-Loop Identification Error, the deployment-induced Action Error, and the continuous Tracking Error. Through discrete-time sensitivity analysis, this work formalizes how offline-learned parameters locally guarantee a trajectory divergence upon deployment, degrading performance due to local loss geometry. To mitigate this distribution shift, we propose actionable design policies centered on time-scale separated online adaptation. These mechanisms are validated through ablation studies on a nonlinear Duffing oscillator, demonstrating that bounded continuous learning successfully mitigates trajectory divergence whereas static deployments fail, offering concrete guidelines for practitioners deploying machine learning components in safety-critical feedback systems.

papers.title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
papers.abstract: Neural networks often learn low-frequency components before high-frequency ones --- a phenomenon called spectral bias or termed F-principle. Many numerical studies have demonstrated this phenomenon, and theoretical studies have sought to explain it. However, several goals remain insufficiently addressed: (1) explaining spectral bias asymptotically, including its origin and why the preferred components are generally sinusoidal; (2) extending the explanation to general activation functions, such as sigmoid and ReLU; (3) making weak assumptions about the data distribution; (4) avoiding aliasing effects, such as those arising in finite-domain Fourier analysis; and (5) developing a theoretical framework applicable to arbitrary networks. We address these goals theoretically by analyzing the eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes of the dynamics matrix H, which arises when we expand the network output as a general Fourier series (GFS) in an orthogonal polynomial basis and express the gradient-descent dynamics of the GFS coefficients as ordinary differential equations. The graded structure of H enables an intuitive explanation of spectral bias, while orthogonal polynomial theory helps us analyze how learning bias depends on the activation function and, potentially, the network architecture.

papers.title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling
papers.abstract: Accurate atomistic simulations of materials under electric fields require long-range electrostatics and electrical-response modeling at length scales beyond the reach of conventional first-principles methods. Yet these capabilities remain difficult to reconcile with the scalability of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Strictly local models enable efficient spatial parallelization but neglect long-range interactions, whereas existing electrostatic extensions introduce global dependencies that hinder distributed computation. Here, we overcome this limitation by analytically separating the long-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges (BECs) into a global electrostatics calculation and strictly local derivatives of learned latent charges. This formulation preserves the spatial decomposability of equivariant MLIPs while enabling distributed evaluation of energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across different boundary conditions. Implemented as DPA4C-LR on the \texttt{nvalchemi} platform, the framework scales to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at approximately twice the computational cost of its short-range backbone. Trained on energies and forces, DPA4C-LR accurately infers BECs and reproduces the field-dependent infrared spectra of water. We further demonstrate its capabilities by recovering the characteristic slim polarization hysteresis of relaxor \ce{Pb(Mg_{1/3}Nb_{2/3})O3}, which is obscured by finite-size effects in smaller simulations; predicting a room-temperature field-driven ionic conductivity of $6.8 \pm 0.7$~mS/cm in amorphous \ce{Li_{0.9}NbO_{0.9}Cl_{4.1}}; and modeling interfacial thermal transport across Si/diamond interfaces with slab-corrected electrostatics. By combining long-range physics, electrical-response inference, and distributed computation, this framework extends predictive atomistic modeling toward device-relevant length scales.
